open_prs.title: P0-056: scoped native interface for AIRON integration
open_prs.body:
AIR​ON needs to reuse the existing SYNTRIASS retrieval and procedural engine while retaining its source and ownership in AIP. This adds a bounded owner-local JSON process interface over SqliteCorpus and Runtime::invoke, plus authorized document deletion through the existing SQLite/FTS triggers. It provides no model/inference fallback, and consequential operations remain refused.

Local validation: the original native runtime baseline passed 201 tests; AIRON's 20 integration tests passed against the built bridge and real Docling, including authorization, signed-suite rejection, source invalidation, rollback and tamper handling. The broader native attempt stopped on the existing PTRACE_TRACEME-dependent launch test on this restricted host (78/79 vanian-sovereign library checks passed). Format/static checks and exact Git tree comparison are retained. See docs/integrations/AIRON_P0_056_INTERFACE.md.

The trust root is the local OS account and provisioned identity files. This is not enterprise authentication, independent observation or redistribution permission. The external AIRON adapter owns request serialization and signed state anchors. Draft only; no automatic merge. Base is the unmerged teaching branch, not main.

open_prs.title: aip-edge: count one socket as one corroboration, however many times it is read
open_prs.body:
Fixes #18. This is a **product bug, not a test-isolation bug**: under socket churn, the edge reference counted one connection as two (and up to four) corroborations. The test that caught it — `t10_and_t11`, "one connection observed once must not read as two corroborations" — is **unchanged**, as is every other existing assertion.

## Root cause

`/proc/net/tcp` is **not an atomic snapshot**. The kernel produces it through `seq_file` across several `read()` calls and resumes each call by position in the socket hash table. When other sockets are created or closed between those calls, a row is emitted twice.

Shown independently of this code: reading the table while other threads churned loopback sockets gave a repeated inode in **29 of 400** reads, against **0 of 400** with no churn.

From there the bug was inherited down the chain:

1. `aip-observe::observe_sockets` joins the table to the instance's descriptors by inode. The join is correct, but a repeated row survives it.
2. `aip-edge-observer` emitted **one observation per row**.
3. Each became a record, and `aip-effect` counts **records**.

A captured failure showed four `ProcNetTable` records for one socket: same inode, same local port 51406, same remote port 41879. It needs churn, which is why it never appeared serially and only when the file's scenarios ran together.

## How I got there, including the hypotheses that were wrong

| hypothesis | result |
|---|---|
| per-PID temp state shared by concurrent scenarios | **refuted** — the directory combines PID, tag and an atomic nonce |
| the cross-execution scenario observing the shared test process | **refuted** — 0 of 30 barrier-synchronised rounds |
| CPU contention | **refuted** — 0 of 10 under 4 busy loops |
| the replayed batch escaping deduplication | **refuted** — the replayed copy was deduplicated; the extra records were inside one real batch |
| duplicate rows from a non-atomic table read under churn | **confirmed** — captured directly, and reproduced in isolation |

The fresh-build dependence turned out to be incidental. `ensure_sibling_binaries` sits behind a `OnceLock`, so on a fresh build all 14 tests block on one `cargo build` and are then released together, which maximises socket churn.

## The fix: two layers, because either alone leaves a hole

**`aip-edge-observer`** — emit one observation per distinct socket. Rows equal in every field the table reports (protocol, endpoints, state, inode) are one socket. Rows that share an inode but **differ in state are kept**: the socket changed state between reads, and both are what the kernel said. The reply now reports `repeated-rows N`, so the deduplication is visible, not silent.

**`aip-edge/src/effect.rs`** — `assess_effect` counts one observation per distinct socket per observed process instance before handing records to `aip-effect`. This covers what the observer cannot see — the same open socket described in **two different batches** by an observer that polls more than once — so the verifier doesn't depend on every observer deduplicating. Two design constraints:

- **Different instances are never merged**, so one execution's evidence can't stand in for another's.
- The representative of a group is its **first member inside the effect window**, else its first. `aip-effect` filters by window afterwards, and keeping an out-of-window duplicate while dropping an in-window one would turn a real corroboration into `OutsideWindow`.

`aip-effect` itself is untouched: it is domain-neutral and has no socket identity to deduplicate on.

## Tests: one per path

| layer | test |
|---|---|
| observer | repeated row is one socket · many repeats still one · two genuine sockets both kept · one socket in two states keeps both · order preserved · non-socket passthrough |
| effect | repeat within one snapshot · same socket in two batches · four repeats · in-window sighting kept when the first is outside · **two genuine sockets still count twice** · **identical sockets on different instances never merged** · non-socket never collapsed · order preserved |

**Falsified:** with the deduplication disabled, exactly the five counting tests fail and the three over-collapsing guards (in bold, plus non-socket) still pass.

## Proof: same harness before and after

The release `end_to_end` binary, its 14 tests running concurrently, under 4 threads of loopback churn, on a fresh build:

| | runs | failed |
|---|---|---|
| **base code** | 60 | **4** (2 × `t10`, 2 × `two_honest_runs_agree…` seeing 3 and 5 records where 2 were expected) |
| **this fix, concurrent** | **200** | **0** |
| **this fix, serial** (`--test-threads=1`) | 50 | 0 |
| barrier probe, all 8 scenario kinds released together | before 130 / after 100 replay checks | before **5** / after **0** |
| `tests/adversarial.rs` under churn | 50 | 0 |

A pass after the fix only means something because the identical harness made the base fail. Both after-run binaries were confirmed to contain the fix (the observer carries `repeated-rows`, the test binary `distinct_socket_observations`) and were rebuilt immediately before the runs.

**All four baseline failures had this one cause.** The second symptom — two honest runs disagreeing on record count — is the same repeated row inflating an honest run's records.

## Impact on published figures: none change

Checked three ways:

1. **Code path.** `aip-corroborate`, `aip-probe` and `aip-collector` never call `observe_sockets`, read socket tables through it, or use the effect assessment.
2. **Matching.** `aip-corroborate` pairs one-to-one: each external exec claims at most one AIP exec.
3. **Sealed evidence, recounted:**
   - **bpftrace 113 agreed / auditd 112 agreed** — no exec appears in two agreements (by pid, image and time) and no external event does either. The 25 repeated PIDs are all `env` then `true`: `env` execs `true` in the same process, two genuine execs. The AIP-only entries are the harness's own `date` and `tee`.
   - **LangGraph 167** — recounts to 167 (79 `Exec` + 88 `Fork`), every event distinct, across 2 batches with no repeated sequence.
   - Neither sealed archive contains a single `ProcNetTable` observation. Their events come from the scheduler, socket-state and socket-send tracepoints and the proc connector.

## Not changed, and why

`aip-observe::observe_sockets`, where the repeated row first appears. It is a different crate with other callers (`ghost-demo`, `aip-observe`'s own tests), and outside the permission for this fix. The proposal — deduplicate rows by full identity inside the join, and count repeats alongside `malformed` — is on #18 for whoever owns it.

## Also in this branch

`9b81098` is #16's namespace fix, cherry-picked byte-identical (`git cherry-pick -x c39fc1f`). This branch is cut from the base, which does not yet have it, so without it CI would go red on the three `vanian-sovereign` sandbox tests that #16 fixes. Disjoint files; it becomes a no-op if #16 merges first. `trivy` will stay red: that failure comes from the base and is tracked in #15.

`cargo fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` clean on both crates. Every `aip-edge` and `aip-edge-observer` test binary passes; `vanian-sovereign` 98/0.

open_prs.title: Give the probe pod the runtime's default seccomp profile
open_prs.body:
The one finding in #15 that is genuinely fixable. The probe DaemonSet ran with `hostPID` and `hostNetwork` and **no pod-level security context at all** — so no syscall filter. It now sets `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault` at pod level.

`hostPID`, `hostNetwork` and the `/proc`, tracefs and cgroupfs mounts are unchanged: they are what a host observer is, and the decision about how to treat them is still open on #15.

## What this does not do

**It does not turn `trivy filesystem scan` green**, and isn't trying to. All four findings, KSV-0118 included, live in the retained render `validation/enterprise/results/HELM_20261028T103133Z/template-enabled.yaml` — evidence of a past run, which this PR does not touch. The live template isn't meaningfully scanned at all: trivy can't parse Helm placeholders, so it reports **0 findings for this file whatever it contains**.

**"KSV-0118 cleared" is not the evidence for this change either.** I measured it on a scratch copy of the render with trivy 0.76.2:

| pod-level `securityContext` | findings |
|---|---|
| none (as is) | KSV-0009, KSV-0010, **KSV-0118**, KSV-0121 |
| `seccompProfile: RuntimeDefault` | KSV-0009, KSV-0010, KSV-0121 |
| `runAsUser: 0` — a control that hardens nothing | KSV-0009, KSV-0010, KSV-0121 |

The rule only checks that a pod context is non-empty, so it can be silenced without improving anything. The test added here therefore asserts the specific property — `seccompProfile: type: RuntimeDefault` — **on the probe's own pod spec**, since a pod context elsewhere in the file would satisfy a bare substring check without protecting the probe. Falsified: with the chart change reverted, the assertion fails. The cosmetic control above would fail it too.

## Not verified on a cluster — please read before relying on it

The `sched` sensor needs `perf_event_open`; the `connector` sensor needs a `NETLINK_CONNECTOR` socket. Whether a runtime's default seccomp profile permits `perf_event_open` to a container holding `CAP_PERFMON` — without the broad administrative capability this chart deliberately never grants — **depends on the runtime and its version**, and I have no cluster or probe image to test it with.

If a sensor fails to open under this profile, the probe must report reduced coverage, never silent success. That needs confirming on the target runtime. The template says so inline; the chart is already annotated `vanian.example/validation: unvalidated-template`, and `test_packaging.py` already states that rendering and cluster behaviour require separate acceptance. If you would rather not take a hardening change you can't yet run, closing this is a reasonable call — it changes no check result.

## Verification

| check | result |

open_prs.title: Refuse when the sandbox namespaces cannot be created, and grant them in CI
open_prs.body:
Makes the three failing `vanian-sovereign` sandbox tests **actually execute** on GitHub runners rather than be skipped, per the decision on #14. It also fixes the production defect that made them fail, which turned out to be the more serious half.

## The defect

`unshare` is a child process. A kernel that refuses the namespaces does not make `spawn` fail — unshare execs fine, fails its own setup, writes the reason to stderr and exits non-zero. The runner treated that as the **tool's** exit status and signed a run record for it.

Three consequences, all live on `ubuntu-24.04` runners:

1. **A signed evidence record claimed a tool had run and exited 1 when nothing ran at all.** This crate exists to make execution evidence trustworthy, so this is the one that matters.
2. `tampered_exit_code_rejected` tampers a genuine record **to** `Code(1)`. Because a failed unshare also produced `Code(1)`, the tampered bundle was byte-identical to the real one — the verifier was *correct* to accept it. That test was failing because the evidence really had become indistinguishable, not because the verifier was broken.
3. `sandbox_environment_is_empty` and `deadline_kills_the_tool` **passed**, because a tool that never runs produces no output and a non-zero exit, which is exactly what each asserted. Two tests were measuring a broken sandbox and reporting success. The CI tally of "16 passed, 3 failed" was flattering.

## The fix

`SandboxRunner::probe_namespaces` runs `unshare` with the **same flags** over `/bin/true` and requires exit 0, **before the one-shot decision is consumed**. A refusal is `RunError::SandboxUnavailable` carrying the kernel's reason: nothing is consumed, nothing is signed, and the caller's authorization survives a run that never happened.

Not cached — a cached verdict would be wrong for the life of the process if an operator changed the sysctl underneath it. The cost is one `/bin/true` fork against a run already bounded by `timeout_ms`.

## Granting the capability in CI

Ubuntu 24.04 ships `kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`, which denies unprivileged user namespaces to the user `validation/ci/with_cgroup.sh` runs the tests as. That script now sets it to `0` and preflights the namespaces as that user, failing with the kernel's reason if they are still refused — the same discipline the freezer preflight beside it already applies. One change covers `fmt · clippy · test`, the release perf-gate run and `coverage`, since all three go through that wrapper.

**It does not run the tests as root**, which was the other option offered. Root can create the namespaces, but it also changes what these tests measure — file modes, capability checks, what a sandboxed process may touch — so a pass as root would not be evidence about the unprivileged path the product actually uses.

**And the tests do not skip.** A runtime skip in the built-in Rust harness *is* a pass: `#[ignore]` is resolved at compile time, and a test that prints a reason and returns early is counted `ok`. There is no way to report a skipped sandbox test as `SKIPPED` in the summary, so the skip-with-reason fallback could not have met its own stated condition ("counted as SKIPPED, never passed") in this harness. Fixing the environment was the better of the two, and it is why I did not build the fallback.

## Verification

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p vanian-sovereign` | **98 passed, 0 failed** |
| `tests/agent_execution.rs` | **22 passed** (was 19) |
| `cargo fmt -p vanian-sovereign --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p vanian-sovereign --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| outer + extracted inner `with_cgroup.sh` | `bash -n` clean |
| the preflight `unshare` invocation, run in isolation | exit 0 |

Three new tests:

- `the_namespace_probe_succeeds_where_the_sandbox_works` — asserts the precondition directly, so a restricted kernel names the cause **once** instead of producing five confusing assertion failures.
- `an_unshare_that_fails_its_own_setup_is_not_mistaken_for_a_tool_exit` — `/bin/false` stands in for a refusing kernel; asserts `SandboxUnavailable` **and** that the one-shot decision was not consumed. This is the regression test for the defect, and it needs no special kernel.
- `the_probe_refuses_when_unshare_is_not_executable`.

`sandbox_environment_is_empty` now asserts the tool reached exit 0 *before* asserting its output was empty, so it can never again pass on an absence.

### What I could not verify here, stated plainly

**The CI change is verified by CI.** This container runs as uid 0 on a non-AppArmor kernel, so neither the sysctl branch nor an unprivileged refusal is reproducible in it — the namespace preflight passes here trivially. I have syntax-checked both the outer script and the inner `bash -c` program and run the preflight command in isolation, but whether the sysctl relaxation is sufficient on the runner image is a claim only this PR's own CI run can settle. If it is not, the preflight will now say so with the kernel's reason instead of leaving five tests to fail obscurely, and I will follow up here.

A new crate README documents both host preconditions, why a refusal is not skipped, and this defect.

Refs #15 (that issue tracks the separate, inherited `trivy` failure on this branch).

open_prs.title: Model resolver, dataset setup, pinned Python env
open_prs.body:
Shared prerequisites for the demo work, split out so both demo sessions build on one copy. Three defects with the same shape: something correct on exactly one machine, failing everywhere else with a message that did not say why.

## 1. Model paths (X1)

**Seven** hard-coded instances of `/home/claude/vanian-build/...` across five scripts — five model directories, two `llama-server` paths — plus three duplicate copies of the SHA-256 digests that could drift apart. Every one of those scripts was unrunnable on any machine but the original build host.

| file | was |
|---|---|
| `run_demo.sh` | model + server, inline, no override at all |
| `run_holdout_v02.sh` | model dir + server, no override; plus a duplicated digest |
| `run_atomic.sh` | bad default, duplicated digests, second server path in `exec` |
| `run_all.sh` | bad default behind `MODELS`, plus the digest table |
| `mkconfig.py` | bad default for the model dir, the server, **and** the sidecar interpreter |

`deploy/syntriass/models.manifest.json` is now the single source of truth — four pinned models, digests cross-checked between `run_all.sh` and `BASELINES.md`, each with the provenance of its pin recorded so no digest is just a number somebody typed. `resolve_model.py` resolves against it with precedence `MODELS` > `SYNTRIASS_BUNDLE/models` > `/opt/syntriass/current/models`. Every pre-existing override is preserved, and the default is where `README.md` §3 already installs — not a path invented here.

SHA-256 is authoritative and subsumes the documented size. A mismatch is **refused**, never warned about: a demo that quietly runs different weights produces numbers nobody can reproduce. Hashing 1.8 GiB is not free, so `path` does not hash unless asked; anything recording a measurement passes `--verify`. Exit codes are the contract — 2 caller error, 3 not staged, 4 integrity, 5 provenance unverified.

**Provenance fails closed.** No model card was reachable from the sandbox, so every entry's `source_url` and `licence` is `UNVERIFIED_NO_NETWORK` and `resolve_model.py provenance` exits 5 for it — a staging script cannot download an unverified model by accident. The three additional models wanted (a 7B-class, IBM Granite, Mistral-7B-Instruct) sit under `not_yet_pinned` rather than being added with a licence recalled from memory.

## 2. The sidecar's data is gitignored, and nothing said so (X6)

`.gitignore:11` is a blanket `*.jsonl`, so the interpretation sidecar's seeded training data is absent on a fresh clone although that dataset's `MANIFEST.json` **is** tracked. The sidecar trains from it at startup, so it died, and the runtime reported only:

```
Inference: sidecar reply missing or oversized
```

naming neither the file nor the cause. The traceback was captured all along — into a log file the runtime itself creates — and nothing pointed at it.

`verify_datasets.py` regenerates the seeded dataset and checks every split against the digest pinned in the tracked manifest. It reads that manifest **from git, not disk**: a regenerated run rewrites `MANIFEST.json`, so comparing the working copy against itself would pass unconditionally. All five splits reproduce byte-identically, which is why committing the data is unnecessary. A split that does not match is a *different* dataset — refused, non-zero exit, never a warning.

Both layers of the message are fixed. The runtime now prints the sidecar's own diagnosis end to end:

```
Inference: sidecar reply missing or oversized; the sidecar exited (exit status: 3)
  stderr log: .../state/sidecar.log
  last stderr from the sidecar:
    sidecar: required dataset is missing, so the interpretation model cannot be trained.
      missing file: .../maintenance-priority-v2/train.jsonl
      cause: .gitignore excludes *.jsonl, so this seeded dataset is not in the repository.
      fix (environment and data): deploy/syntriass/setup_env.sh
      fix (data only):            python3 -I deploy/syntriass/verify_datasets.py --generate
```

One race was found and fixed **in the production path, not papered over in the test**: a dying child has not necessarily flushed stderr when `try_wait()` first returns, so the most valuable case — exited at startup *with a reason* — could report an empty log. There is now a bounded 500 ms settle before the log is read, short enough not to delay a genuinely hung sidecar. Found because the test was flaky under the parallel suite while passing in isolation; the suite now runs 95/0 three times consecutively.

## 3. The documented Python requirement understated reality (X7)

README §1 said "Python ≥ 3.10 with numpy", but `extractors.py` imports `sklearn` **lazily** inside `fit()`, so the real requirement only surfaced at sidecar startup. `requirements.lock` pins the full set with hashes — derived from wheels actually downloaded for cp311 x86-64, not transcribed — and `setup_env.sh` installs with `pip install --require-hashes`, so a file that does not match is refused rather than installed. Bundle wheels are preferred; PyPI is the fallback only when no wheel directory is present.

`fastembed` is deliberately absent, with the reason recorded in the lock: it is imported only inside `_embedder()` for the `embed` mode and would fetch `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` from Hugging Face at first use. A network call cannot be part of an offline path.

It installs into a **venv**, and that is not tidiness. Installing system-wide failed outright: the lock pins `packaging 26.3`, Debian ships 24.0 with no `RECORD` file, and pip cannot replace it. Found by actually running the reinstall rather than assuming it would work. `mkconfig.py`'s hard-coded `"python": "/usr/local/bin/python3"` — the same defect family as the model paths — now prefers that venv, falls back to the running interpreter, and takes a `SIDECAR_PYTHON` override.

## Evidence

Re-run from the lock-installed venv **after** uninstalling the hand-installed `numpy`/`scikit-learn`/`pytest` and confirming the sidecar fails without them, so none of this rests on packages added by hand.

| check | result |
|---|---|
| `deploy/syntriass/tests/test_resolve_model.py` | 23 passed |
| `deploy/syntriass/tests/test_setup.py` | 21 passed |
| `research/capability-learning/tests` | 53 passed |
| `research/system-one/tests` (from its own dir, as its README documents) | 18 passed |
| `cargo test -p syntriass-runtime --locked` | 8 binaries, **95 passed, 0 failed** (×3 consecutive) |
| `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |
| `cargo fmt --check` | exit 0 |

Two of the seven model-path instances were **missed by the search pass and caught only by the test**, which asserts over an explicit caller list rather than trusting a grep. That is why it is written that way.

## Notes for review

- `research/compute-memory/bench/offline.sh` is **deliberately untouched** — it is the provenance for the published v0.2 results and is byte-identical on this branch.
- `BASELINES.md` is corrected: it cited `bench/run_all.sh` as where the model digests are pinned, which this change moves to the manifest. The values are unchanged, and `run_all.sh` keeps a mirror that a test asserts agrees.
- The venv and the staged wheel directory are gitignored — both reproduce from the lock, neither is committed.
- This branch contains **only** the shared prerequisites. Demo-specific work and per-session checklists stay on the demo branches.

open_prs.title: Add evidence-first enterprise service onboarding model benchmarked against WitnessAI
open_prs.body:
## Purpose
Benchmark the **publicly documented enterprise service model** of WitnessAI (Observe / Control / Protect, isolated deployments, connectors, APIs and a CISO console), then make a **distinct, evidence-first VANIAN customer onboarding path** on top of PR #7.

## What changed
- Added `docs/enterprise/SERVICE_DELIVERY_MODEL.md` with sourced comparison, differentiated value proposition, proposed service catalog, customer lifecycle, explicit availability limits and institutional acceptance gates.
- Added `integrations/service_delivery/service_onboard.py`: offline, standard-library JSON onboarding plan validator; no network calls or private keys.
- Added non-secret sample manifest, 16 negative/positive Python unit tests and a CI workflow.
- Linked onboarding model from the bank integration guide and enterprise deployment package.

## Security boundaries
The planner *rejects* unqualified agentless network discovery and prompt protection claims, automatic containment, transaction gating, non-Linux observation, colocated probe/collector hosts, shared administration, unsupported HSM custody and prompt/transaction-body capture. It always returns `institutional_pilot: NOT_VERIFIED` and unavailable live observation coverage. Validating JSON is **not** security validation.

## Validation
Locally ran `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s integrations/service_delivery/tests -v`: **16 passed, 0 failed**, and generated a sample JSON report. The new workflow is configured to run these same checks in CI; no GitHub Actions success is claimed before it executes.

## What is not built
No WitnessAI-compatible proprietary network connector, no comprehensive shadow-agent discovery, no inline prompt injection/DLP engine, no managed SaaS or production single-tenant deployment, and no full same-run signed authorization/kernel/gateway/reconciliation validation. No independent bank pilot, security certification or customer adoption is claimed.

Review against the enterprise-integration feature branch; do not merge into `main` automatically.

## Additional customer-facing functionality
- `integrations/service_delivery/posture_report.py` reuses the actual enterprise Python SDK, with institution-scoped Reader credentials, HTTPS-only transport, no redirects, bounded first-page read and no raw evidence export. It inspects authenticated `/v1/access`, packet-listed agents, `/v1/coverage` and `/v1/health`.
- Six additional contract tests prevent API-reported health/agent declarations from being misrepresented as independent runtime coverage or identity proof. Local total: **22 Python tests passed**, no live bank service was contacted.

## GitHub Actions qualification
The new PR's GitHub Actions attempts all stopped within seconds, with no executed steps and no downloadable job logs. This does **not** establish a test failure in the source, but there is no green CI evidence for this PR. Troubleshoot the repository/runner/workflow availability before merge; preserve the draft state.

open_prs.title: Add tested agent interoperability with native authority and gateway correlation
open_prs.body:
VANIAN needs to preserve external identity and governance claims while independently checking the native evidence that supports them. This adds optional interoperability adapters, real ADK/A2A/Microsoft-governed ContextForge execution, native offline authority-chain verification, and a read-only comparison of the exact ACS-reported tool input with the signed gateway request. **The complete institutional same-run milestone remains open.**

Stacked on draft PR #8 at exact base `e3aa195def7524d6ec84d37a934beebe18b6c794`, which already combines #6 and #7. No draft is merged. Historical RBI evidence and cryptographic signing formats are preserved.

### Resulting behavior
- Pinned-key JWT/JWT-SVID references retain issuer, tenant, provenance and unresolved logical-agent mappings.
- Official A2A SDK uses pinned HTTPS/mTLS origins, card provenance and a clearly labeled signed task profile with durable local replay protection.
- OPA remains the policy evaluator. ADK callbacks, native Microsoft ACS results and OpenShell OCSF imports retain their source boundaries.
- Existing ContextForge/Rust signatures attest to actual gateway-received parameters.
- `verify_authority_reference` verifies expectation signatures, exact native root/hop references, signatures/attenuation, leaf, action scope and validity at issuance. Known delegators cannot silently become root issuers.
- New public-key-only `aip-tool-receipt compare-request` recomputes the original native commitment and compares agent, decision, tool and request IDs. It preserves Forwarded/Refused/Failed dispositions and establishes no authority or execution.
- The optional ACS bridge calls the pinned upstream input-identity implementation. For its explicit untransformed integer-JSON pre-tool profile, it checks the native input/snapshot/context and compares the exact arguments against the verified receipt. Policy producer/version authenticity and logical-agent mapping remain unestablished.
- The live workload translates the model's synthetic record selection **before** ACS evaluation and sends the evaluated arguments to ContextForge with the same request ID.
- Missing observations still return CannotProve, including when native authority verifies. The read-only host preflight exposes unavailable observation prerequisites.

### Actual validation
Latest continuation, code head `9d52c68c93e634479dd82b012f7ef941b796d551`:
- Two fresh genuine ADK/A2A/Microsoft/ContextForge lab runs completed. The retained final run has four model generations, 28 gateway checks/receipts and five live authentication/governance negatives.
- The final run's ACS-reported input matches its signed gateway request offline. All 18 captured adapter source hashes match the retained code.
- Native gateway suite: 34 passed, including eight new public-key-only CLI adversarial tests.
- Native Microsoft archive suite: 25 passed using the installed pinned SDK and real Rust verifier; no mock hashing, policy engine or receipt signatures.
- Optional adapter suite: 47 passed. Revised ACS Rego scope: four passed.
- All 28 new gateway signatures verify offline; altered commitments are refused.
- Workspace-wide Clippy (all targets/features, warnings denied) and formatting passed.

Earlier retained validation:
- Actual OPA mTLS allow/deny/no-client-certificate checks and four Rego tests pass.
- Initial scoped native suites: 446 passed, one ignored. Authority continuation: 183 passed, one ignored, including 12 new adversarial tests; offline composition example: five passed. **These suite totals overlap and must not be added.**
- Python SDK: 76 passed in its prescribed clean environment; TypeScript: two; MCP boundaries: nine; RBI control-flow: 17; packaging/harness/SQL and historical archive regression passed.
- **Full local Cargo workspace run remains failed:** 3078 passed, 161 failed, eight ignored across 28 failed targets. The complete log is retained; scoped success does not reclassify it as green.

**Exact-head remote CI is blocked:** all 12 jobs failed with runner ID 0 and no test steps, including the new pinned-native-SDK offline job. The provider reason is not exposed; no remote tests are claimed as executed.
- [Interoperability](https://github.com/richardrich999888-rgb/AIP-agent-identity-protocol-/actions/runs/40720802349)
- [Main CI](https://github.com/richardrich999888-rgb/AIP-agent-identity-protocol-/actions/runs/40720802391)

### Evidence and remaining guarantees
[Validation report](https://github.com/richardrich999888-rgb/AIP-agent-identity-protocol-/blob/feature/vanian-agent-governance-interoperability/docs/interoperability/VALIDATION_REPORT.md) and [new live/offline archive](https://github.com/richardrich999888-rgb/AIP-agent-identity-protocol-/tree/feature/vanian-agent-governance-interoperability/validation/interoperability/results/20261028-receipt-join) retain transcripts, native records, signed receipts, public lab anchors, source hashes, adversarial results and reproduction commands. Earlier archives remain unchanged.

ACS input hashes are unkeyed. A fabricated policy record can be content-consistent with an authentic receipt, so the bridge explicitly refuses to promote self-declared source authenticity. Tenant-scoped gateway authority and tool aliases require assessor configuration; receipt v1 has no tenant field. Transforms, approvals and additional native profiles remain insufficient for this comparison.

No independent institutional ExpectedExecution is supplied for the model operation; separate comparator authorizations remain labeled fixtures. Same-run workload/logical-agent binding, kernel capture, independent collector signatures and enterprise admission/readback remain open. Remote A2A kernel execution remains UNOBSERVED. SPIRE/OpenShell runtime validation is blocked by host prerequisites.

Exact upstream pins and licenses remain in the lock/inventory. ADK A2A is experimental; Microsoft compatibility SDK 0.4.0b0 uses native ACS alpha.4. No upstream source is vendored by this increment. Full A2A TCK/MCP conformance, production support, independent security certification and vendor endorsement are not claimed.

open_prs.title: Import: OrbitalTrust accountability layer (side-by-side, not merged)
open_prs.body:
## Summary

Imports the OrbitalTrust accountability layer from `ASC-space` into this repo under `orbitaltrust-accountability/`, as an **import, not a merge**. Nothing under `aip-standalone/` is touched — the two codebases overlap in part (evidence packets, identity/delegation, the verification CLI, the hash-chained audit trail) and complement each other in part (this brings `ot-sentinel` out-of-band reconciliation, `ot-mcp-gateway`, a durable tamper-evident authority store, a TypeScript console layer + browser/WASM verifier, and a Python SDK proven byte-identical against the Rust core), and picking a winner on the overlap is a maintainer decision this PR does not make for you.

114 files, 35,440 lines, with a SHA-256 `MANIFEST.md` of every imported file for integrity checking.

## Type

feat

## The integration question this PR raises and does not answer

The two hash-chain constructions are **not wire-compatible**: `aip-core` chains raw 32-byte digests; `ot-accountability-core` chains `SHA-256(previous ‖ canonical JSON)` as hex. Both are sound constructions; a packet sealed by one will not verify under the other. Reconciling them (or deciding not to) is left to a maintainer.

## What's new here that isn't in `aip-standalone/` today

- **`ot-sentinel`** — out-of-band reconciliation. AIP's funnel proves what went through it; it has no answer for an agent that declines to use the funnel at all, because inline enforcement cannot see its own bypass. The sentinel reconciles independent sensor observations against what the ledger sealed, across 11 detectors, under a warrant standard where automatic containment requires arithmetic proof rather than suspicion. Ships with a runnable binary.
- **`ot-mcp-gateway`** — the funnel on the MCP wire, sealing every `tools/call` before it reaches the upstream server.
- **A durable, tamper-evident authority store** — an append-only hash-chained journal (`authority_journal.rs`) rather than a database, so the record that decides who may do what cannot be silently rewritten.
- **A TypeScript console layer and browser/WASM verifier**, and a **Python SDK** proven byte-identical against the Rust core.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated — the imported crates carry their own suites (`ot-accountability-core` 56, `ot-mcp-gateway` 80, `ot-sentinel` 114, TypeScript 117), verified passing in the source workspace at import time. **Not yet wired into this repo's CI or `cargo test --all`** — see below.
- [x] Docs updated — `orbitaltrust-accountability/README.md` and `MANIFEST.md` added; existing docs untouched.
- [x] Security reviewed — no secrets committed; purely additive, no authn/tenant surface in `aip-standalone/` is touched.
- [x] Backwards compatible — nothing under `aip-standalone/` is modified.
- [x] Migration notes — N/A, no schema or behavior change to `aip-service`.
- [ ] `cargo fmt --check` / `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — **does not yet apply**: the imported crates inherit dependency versions from the source workspace's `workspace-Cargo.toml`, which travels with them but is not wired into this repo's Cargo workspace.
